signal: BoomPop raised $41M led by Wing VC to scale its AI-native event planning platform into the corporate group travel market

email.body1:
Greg, saw BoomPop closed $41M to scale its AI-native event platform into corporate group travel.

Post-raise, the in-market list grows faster than the team can act on it, and the lag between a signal firing and a rep touching the account is where pipeline leaks. Our AI SDR turns signals into researched, personalized outreach autonomously: 3-5x more meetings per rep, no new hires.

I built a signal play for BoomPop off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Greg, quick follow-up for BoomPop.

As volume scales, data hygiene and slow follow-up quietly drag down conversion, and the measurable lift hides in the gaps. Our built-in best practices alone tend to lift response rates 50 to 70 percent.

Worth 15 minutes? I'll walk you through a teardown of your current outbound and three things I'd change, plus how every email auto-logs to the CRM so attribution stays clean.
email.body3:
Greg, last bit of proof for BoomPop.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how BoomPop's reply rate likely compares to other recently funded startups. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Greg, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If tightening signal-to-action and outbound efficiency isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Timing is everything right after a raise, and the scale-up stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a RevOps motion? I'll tailor it to BoomPop either way.
